content:
According to Bloomberg's latest report, Apple will launch a brand-new "Apple Upgrade" rental plan in the United States later this month. The report describes it as "one of the most significant changes in the company's history of selling devices."

Here's how the plan works.

Lower monthly hardware costs

Apple has partnered with Klarna to support the new Apple Upgrade plan. Customers must undergo a soft credit check.

According to reports, Apple Upgrade will operate "like a subscription service," applicable to purchases of iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch. However, the plan comes with certain restrictions. Reports indicate that the Apple Watch SE, base-model iPad, iPhone 16, and MacBook Neo are all ineligible for Apple Upgrade.

According to reports, the rental term for iPhone and Apple Watch is 24 months, while for Mac it is 36 months.

Mark Gurman explains:

Apple Upgrade does not include AppleCare service, which differs from the iPhone Upgrade Program. In fact, Bloomberg reports that Apple plans to discontinue new sign-ups for the iPhone Upgrade Program with the launch of Apple Upgrade.

According to reports, Apple Upgrade will officially launch one week from now, on July 28.

Apple raised prices on iPad and Mac last month, and the new iPhones expected in September are also anticipated to see price increases. Apple Upgrade will offer customers an option to cope with rising prices.
